{"documentId": "f_1e468a9d69ea0f0a2001f5", "title": "LLC ground rules (Combo Fighter and whatever else we take)", "name": "LLC ground rules (Combo Fighter and whatever else we take)", "revisionId": "89aa42aa1b", "createdTime": "2026-02-12T23:46:00Z", "modifiedTime": "2026-02-12T23:46:00Z", "text": "LLC ground rules (Combo Fighter and whatever else we take)
This is the lifestyle route I posted about in #executives. The LLC is the new one Blake and I are setting up for the three of us, and anything Harmony Games owns (the games with their art and listings, and the equipment) comes to it only through Sunset's sale, the way I wrote after the call on Wednesday. Services we keep running just move their billing to the LLC.
The plan runs March 1 to May 31.
Domino Delights and Zombie Match come over only if what each made in January, going by the warehouse's daily revenue table, covers what its own hosting bills now, whatever we said about them before. Combo Fighter comes over either way, it's the reason we're doing this. A game that comes over brings what it needs to keep running, its accounts and its player support.
Cost every item at what it bills now, going by whoever runs it, not by what HG used to pay.
What we already decided to keep or cancel for the shutdown in #winddown stays decided.
Pay for anyone who stays on is a separate conversation once we know the running cost; this plan is only what bills us every month, no one-offs or yearly fees.
How things move is on the LLC card on our board.
"}

content.content:
how we split it: each of the three of us carries a third of what the LLC costs a month, March through May. that's everything on the plan that bills monthly, including what one of us already pays for it. whatever one of us already pays personally counts toward his third, and he puts the difference in as cash. put the three shares on the sheet per month.
==
github, dbt and metabase bill to my Kub card from the next bill. I dropped the extra metabase seats so it's the $100 base now, dbt is $100 and github is back to the $48 team plan now that I dropped the extra seat and copilot is off, so $248 a month. I'll carry those through May as my part. the github org itself stays HG's till the data's delivered, I'm just paying the bill, so count it as mine like the other two. bigquery and firebase stay on HG's google account with GA until the data's out, and with CF's tiny volume they cost nothing after that, so there's nothing there for the LLC.
==

Which competitors does this title sit next to?*\\nOn mobile, this title sits closest to:\\n\\u2022 The Sims (Freeplay / Mobile): deep life simulation and expression.\\n\\u2022 Cozy idle sims such as Cats & Soup and similar \\u201cwatch your world run\\u201d games.\\n\\u2022 Lifestyle and decor titles in the home design and fashion space.\\nThe key difference: we are effectively offering a \\u201cquick simulation\\u201d button for Barbie life moments. Every action is designed to resolve in short, satisfying sessions that fit mobile: start a career shift, run a mini day in Barbieland, complete a micro story, then step away.\\nWe borrow some loop structure from idle clickers to keep Barbie\\u2019s world running in the background, but unlike pure idle titles, this game adds roleplay, story context, and character identity on top of those systems. The result is closer to a \\u201csnackable Sims in Barbieland\\u201d than a standard clicker.\\n\\n*2. What gap in the market are you aiming to fill?*\\nThere is no mobile experience today that gives Barbie fans a living, evergreen Barbieland where they can:\\n\\u2022 Collect across the full, ever evolving Barbie universe, not just one product line.\\n\\u2022 Test drive careers, lifestyles, and aesthetics in a low friction, low cost way.\\n\\u2022 Return daily to see their Barbieland grow and change with the brand.\\nThe gap is a \\u201cBarbie lovers universe\\u201d that goes much deeper than a single dress up app or one Dreamhouse. This concept lets fans continuously engage with more facets of Barbie, and live those fantasies digitally at a fraction of the cost of physical collecting, while still driving demand for the physical line.\\n\\n*3. How does this differ from Dreamhouse Adventures, Miniverse, Toca Boca, etc.?*\\n\\u2022 *Dreamhouse Adventures:* Centered on one location and one core fantasy loop. Our concept treats the Dreamhouse as one important module inside a larger Barbieland, with careers, locations, and storylines that expand well beyond the house.\\n\\u2022 *Miniverse:* Focuses on miniature making and ASMR style crafting. We take some sensory inspiration, but our core is life simulation and roleplay: what Barbie does with those worlds once they exist.\\n\\u2022 *Toca Boca:* Fantastic at open ended play for kids, but genre agnostic and not rooted in Barbie\\u2019s IP or audience. We are designing a life sim where the mechanics, aesthetics, and progression are specifically tuned to Barbie\\u2019s brand promise and fanbase.\\nIn short, the IP to genre fit is unique. We are not putting Barbie on top of an existing mechanic. We are building systems that express what Barbie stands for in play: choice of path, creativity, and \\u201cyou can be anything.\\u201d\\n\\n*4. What is the aspirational hook that makes this uniquely Barbie?*\\nThe hook: \\u201cBuild your own Barbieland and live every \\u2018you can be anything\\u2019 fantasy inside it.\\u201d\\nA few pillars support that:\\n\\u2022 *More than one thing to do:* Players can move fluidly between careers, hobbies, fashion, travel, and social stories, just like kids do with the dolls.\\n\\u2022 *Modular and combinable:* Each play module (career tracks, locations, collections, events) snaps together, so your Barbieland feels personal and assembled, not scripted from a single storyline.\\n\\u2022 *Player chosen life paths:* The core loop reinforces the founding philosophy of Barbie: players project their own fantasy into the character and choose their own path, adventure, and profession.\\nThat combination of multi path aspiration plus real systems depth is something only Barbie can authentically own in this space.\\n\\n*5. How does this respond to current cozy sim and lifestyle trends?*\\nThe concept is built directly on top of what is working in cozy and lifestyle sims today:\\n\\u2022 Low pressure, low failure, high comfort play.\\n\\u2022 Strong focus on aesthetics, collection, and decoration that feels shareable and aspirational.\\n\\u2022 Light idle elements that reward coming back often without demanding long sessions.\\n\\u2022 High quality sensory feedback: soft animations, satisfying loops, ASMR like interactions.\\nWe then layer Barbie\\u2019s IP and audience targeting on top:\\n\\u2022 The fantasy and visual language map perfectly to the existing cozy and lifestyle audience, but filtered through Barbie\\u2019s world.\\n\\u2022 The brand gives us a more efficient route to the right players. With Barbie front and center, we can acquire fans at a lower CPI than a generic cozy sim, since the game speaks directly to a known, motivated segment.\\nIn effect, we take Proven cozy and idle patterns, align them tightly with Barbie\\u2019s brand promise, and use the IP to reach the exact audience that already craves this kind of experience.\", \"channel\": \"C09QDMC3UL9\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID\", \"thread_ts\": \"1764867254.892579\"}, {\"ts\": \"1765213543.355689\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"*1. Who is the primary target audience?*\\nThe core audience is teen and adult Barbie fans who already enjoy cozy life sims and light idle games on mobile.\\n\\u2022 Roughly 13 to 55, predominantly female.\\n\\u2022 Strong overlap with players of fashion, home design, and lifestyle sim titles.\\n\\u2022 Comfortable with deeper collection, progression, and event systems, and with free to play economy patterns.\\nA secondary audience is Barbie loving kids around 8 to 12 who will naturally arrive through the brand, siblings, parents, and discovery in app stores. We are not designing the systems around young children, but the experience is friendly and intuitive enough that they can still have fun within safe boundaries.\\nThe product is a free to play idle life sim aimed at a teen plus audience, with meaningful progression, collection, and profession systems to support long term engagement and monetization. Is the game built for teens, young adults, or children?*\\nThe design target is teens and young adults, with adults welcome, and children protected.\\n\\u2022 Systems depth, economy, and long term goals are tuned for players 13 plus who are used to free to play games and can engage with more complex progression and collection.\\n\\u2022 Content, tone, and themes remain family friendly and brand safe, so if an 8 to 12 year old plays alongside an older sibling or parent, the experience still feels appropriate and positive.\\nThis gives Barbie a mobile product that speaks to the broader fandom while staying fully aligned with Mattel standards.\\n\\n*3. *2. What gap in the market are you aiming to fill?*
There is no mobile experience today that gives Barbie fans a living, evergreen Barbieland where they can:
• Collect across the full, ever evolving Barbie universe, not just one product line.
• Test drive careers, lifestyles, and aesthetics in a low friction, low cost way.
• Return daily to see their Barbieland grow and change with the brand.

This concept lets fans continuously engage with more facets of Barbie, and live those fantasies digitally at a fraction of the cost of physical collecting, while still driving demand for the physical line.

• *Dreamhouse Adventures:* Centered on one location and one core fantasy loop. Our concept treats the Dreamhouse as one important module inside a larger Barbieland, with careers, locations, and storylines that expand well beyond the house.
• *Miniverse:* Focuses on miniature making and ASMR style crafting. We take some sensory inspiration, but our core is life simulation and roleplay: what Barbie does with those worlds once they exist.

*4. What is the aspirational hook that makes this uniquely Barbie?*
The hook: “Build your own Barbieland and live every ‘you can be anything’ fantasy inside it.”

• *More than one thing to do:* Players can move fluidly between careers, hobbies, fashion, travel, and social stories, just like kids do with the dolls.

• *Player chosen life paths:* The core loop reinforces the founding philosophy of Barbie: players project their own fantasy into the character and choose their own path, adventure, and profession.

Here's what I'd do. Every issue in the LLC project has my call on it, and the sheet matches the project: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1hqkCJcuj2s-qgzf7YrxXCmRD82paHYRAjiKCFFpIp6I/edit (in my Drive, shared with you and Blake)

**What the LLC takes if Sunset can't sell it**
• **Combo Fighter**: comes over either way, through Sunset's sale. I own it.
• **Domino Delights**: comes over. It made $183.11 in January (warehouse daily revenue) and its prod account bills $140 now, so it covers its own hosting. You're handling it with Sunset. Its player support already goes to the email address.
• **Zombie Match**: stays with HG. It made $0 in January and its AWS account still bills every month. CF doesn't need that account anymore.
• **Services moving to the LLC by March 1**: DD prod AWS and CF's AWS (Blake moves them), and AppsFlyer free tier for CF (you set it up).
• **Everything else stays with HG**: whatever we already cancelled or kept in #winddown, plus the build boxes, the dev/analytics AWS accounts, Figma (lapses Sep 11) and the dev accounts. The listings go with the games. Calm Play isn't used, since the LLC is the new one. The playable vendor is a one-off, so it's not in the plan.

**Monthly cost, March through May: $450**
• Billed to the LLC: DD prod AWS $140 + CF AWS $62 = $202
• Already on Blake's card: Metabase $100 + dbt $100 + GitHub $48 = $248

**Each of us carries $150 a month**
• Me: $150 cash
• You: $150 cash
• Blake: covered by the $248 on his card. That's $98 over his third, so the LLC pays him back $98 a month out of our $300.

Talk Monday.

content.text:
I've made the call on all 37 issues in Linear, put the plan sheet in your Drive and shared it with Leonard and Blake, and replied to Leonard in his DM thread. The project and the sheet match line for line.

**The plan:** the LLC would cost $450 a month from March through May, and each of you carries $150.
- **Billed to the LLC ($202):** Domino Delights' AWS account at $140 and Combo Fighter's at $62.
- **Already on Blake's card ($248):** Metabase $100, dbt $100 and GitHub $48. He's paying these himself through May, as he told you both by email.
- **Shares:** you and Leonard each put in $150 cash. Blake's $248 already covers his third and is $98 over, so the LLC pays him back $98 a month out of your $300.

**What the LLC takes if Sunset can't sell it:**
- **Combo Fighter** comes over either way.
- **Domino Delights** comes over. It made $183.11 in January (warehouse revenue table), which covers its $140 hosting bill.
- **Zombie Match** stays with HG. It made $0 in January and its AWS account still bills every month. This overrides Monday's note that both games would come with Combo Fighter, as the ground rules say it should.

**Where things sit in Linear:**
- **Todo (5), with an assignee:**
  - Combo Fighter (you) and Domino Delights (Leonard), both due when Sunset's sale closes.
  - The two AWS accounts (Blake) and AppsFlyer's free tier for Combo Fighter (Leonard), all due March 1.
- **Done (4):** Blake's three subscriptions, plus Domino Delights player support, which already goes to the email address.
- **Canceled (28):** everything else stays with HG. That covers what was already cancelled or kept in #winddown, the build machines, Figma (prepaid to Sep 11) and the Apple/Google developer accounts. Calm Play is canceled because the ground rules say the LLC is the new one Blake and Leonard are setting up. The $3,750 playable is a one-off, so it isn't in the plan.

Two numbers differ from Leonard's Tuesday draft and from what Blake wrote earlier in Linear; I went with the latest figures from Blake, who runs the accounts:
- Domino Delights' AWS is $140 a month, not about $1,000. Blake said in your DM on Thursday that he'd trimmed it.
- Combo Fighter's AWS is $62, not the $95 in Blake's Linear comment. He shut down an extra backend copy on Thursday night.

I also corrected your draft line that had Figma going to the LLC.

The sheet is "LLC 90 days (plan)": https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1hqkCJcuj2s-qgzf7YrxXCmRD82paHYRAjiKCFFpIp6I/edit
